title: Roof-normalized Ext comparison with signed Koszul dual homology
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, I an ideal, r a natural number and f:Fin r -> A a Koszul-regular sequence generating I [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence, def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex]. Let L be the signed dual [def-sc-koszul-dual-complex]. There is an A-linear equivalence d:Ext^r_A(A/I,A) -> H^r(L), such that for every quasi-isomorphic integer Koszul augmentation epsilon with degree-zero quotient formula and every Ext class x there are a cochain map z:K(f)->A[-r] and a cycle y in L_r with x represented by the roof epsilon^{-1} z followed by the standard single-complex shift isomorphism, d(x)=homologyPi(y), and iCycles(y) equal to the degree -r component of z transported back to K_r. This does not assert any conormal or determinant identification.

source.place: Lemma 48.15.5, finite free Koszul resolution computation; generator independence via Lemma 48.15.4 (Tag 0BQY)

proof.text: Construct the quotient augmentation q of K explicitly: q_0 is I.mkQ after exteriorPower.zeroEquiv, and q_n=0 for n>0. The degree-one boundary has image I because f generates I. Koszul-regularity kills positive homology; finite exterior bases make every K_n projective. Thus K with q is a projective resolution P. Use the construction recorded by new-j3-koszul-projective-resolution, not an arbitrary augmentation chosen from its existence statement. Extend K along embeddingDownNat to E and q to epsilon0. E has zero positive-degree terms and projective nonpositive terms (zero terms are projective), hence is strictly bounded above by 0 and K-projective by lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective. Equivalently the natural-number extension instance in HomotopyCategory/KProjective.lean:126 gives this directly.

Put T=single(A,0), L=koszulDualComplex A r f. In degree n>=0 define e_n(c) to be c.v(-n,0), transported by E.extendXIso.inv and singleObjXSelf.hom; in negative degree both sides are zero. Cochain.toSingleEquiv and its inverse toSingleMk give inverse maps. Cochain.delta_toSingleMk says e_(n+1)(delta c)=(-1)^(n+1) e_n(c) composed with d_(n+1,n), exactly L.d. The maps are A-linear by componentwise evaluation. Let Z be the degree-r cocycles and B the subgroup of coboundaries. Let ZL=ker(L.d r (r+1)), and BL be the range of the incoming differential corestricted to ZL (zero for r=0). The differential equation restricts e_r to a bijection Z to ZL and identifies B with BL, since e_(r-1) is surjective when r>0; degree -1 cochains are zero when r=0. Define on the quotient F([c])=L.homologyPi((L.sc r).moduleCatCyclesIso.inv(e_r(c))). It is well defined since c-c-prime in B gives e_r(c-c-prime) in BL. If F([c])=0 then e_r(c) is in BL by moduleCatHomologyIso and its projection equation, hence c is in B, proving injectivity. Every homology class lifts to ZL via its quotient presentation and then along e_r, proving surjectivity. F is additive and respects A-scalars because e_r and the cycles/projection maps do. Compose F with P.extEquivCohomologyClass to define d on Ext. This is the explicit normalized quotient construction; no information is taken from the existence-only signed-dual equivalence. To establish A-linearity of the Ext leg, represent a class by c. The roof formula and Abelian.Ext.smul_hom identify the roof of a*c with a times the roof of c (Q and the shift maps are A-linear). Injectivity of Ext.homLinearEquiv gives P.extEquivCohomologyClass(a*x)=[a*c], so d(a*x)=a*d(x).

Apply P.extMk_surjective to x in degree r to get a:K_r to A with a composed with d_(r+1,r) zero. Form c=Cocycle.toSingleMk of the transported a. Let z be Cocycle.equivHomShift.symm c followed by the inverse single-complex shift identification to single(A,-r), and y=(L.sc r).moduleCatCyclesIso.inv(e_r(c)). Cochain.toSingleMk_v and the shift component formula show that iCycles(y) is exactly extendXIso.inv followed by z.f(-r) and singleObjXSelf.hom, with no discretionary sign. P.extEquivCohomologyClass_extMk and extMk_hom (equivalently extEquivCohomologyClass_symm_mk_hom) say x.hom is inv(Q epsilon0) followed by Q z and the specified derived single shift inverse; the singleFunctorIsoCompQ conjugations are the identifications in Ext.homLinearEquiv. By the definition of F on quotient classes, d(x)=homologyPi(y). For any epsilon satisfying the displayed quotient equation, equality with epsilon0 holds in degree zero and to_single_hom_ext makes it equality of complex maps. Substitution yields all three required equations for that epsilon. For r=0 the incoming Hom term is zero; for A/I=0 both quotient presentations are zero. No determinant comparison is involved.

proof_origin.place: Repair of X-06699 C3/C4: explicit evaluation on cocycles, boundary-compatible quotient construction, and actual Mathlib Ext roof formulas; no normalization inferred from Nonempty of an equivalence.

theorem exists_koszul_ext_roof_representatives
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (ModuleCat.{u} A)]
    (I : Ideal A) (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A)
    (hreg : RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular f) (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = I) :
    ∃ d : Abelian.Ext (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I)) (ModuleCat.of A A) r ≃ₗ[A]
        (koszulDualComplex A r f).homology r,
      ∀ (ε : (koszulComplex A r f).extend ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat ⟶
          (CochainComplex.singleFunctor (ModuleCat A) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I)))
        [QuasiIso ε],
        (∀ x : ⋀[A]^0 (Fin r →₀ A),
          (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0
            (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I))).hom
            (ε.f 0 (((koszulComplex A r f).extendXIso
              ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat (i := 0) rfl).inv x)) =
          Ideal.Quotient.mk I (exteriorPower.zeroEquiv A (Fin r →₀ A) x)) →
        ∀ x : Abelian.Ext (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I)) (ModuleCat.of A A) r,
          ∃ (z : (koszulComplex A r f).extend ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat ⟶
              (CochainComplex.singleFunctor (ModuleCat A) (-(r : ℤ))).obj
                (ModuleCat.of A A))
            (y : (koszulDualComplex A r f).cycles r),
            x = (Abelian.Ext.homLinearEquiv (R := A)).symm
              (inv (DerivedCategory.Q.map ε) ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map z ≫
                ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctors (ModuleCat A)).shiftIso
                  (r : ℤ) (-(r : ℤ)) 0 (add_neg_cancel (r : ℤ))).inv.app
                    (ModuleCat.of A A)) ∧
            d x = (koszulDualComplex A r f).homologyπ r y ∧
            (koszulDualComplex A r f).iCycles r y = (((koszulComplex A r f).extendXIso
      ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat (i := r) rfl).inv ≫ z.f (-(r : ℤ)) ≫
        (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (-(r : ℤ))
          (ModuleCat.of A A)).hom)
